# Sley

Canonical site: https://sleylang.org/
Organization: Greyforge Labs - https://greyforge.tech/
Public source: https://github.com/GreyforgeLabs/sley/tree/public
License: Apache-2.0
Release: Sley 1.2.0 local release candidate
Status date: 2026-08-27
Discovery role: primary Sley product and citation facts

## Preferred Description

Sley 1.2.0 completes Greyforge Labs' self-hosted, agent-native,
human-readable structural programming line for compiler-mediated software
change.

## Current Architecture Boundary

- Greyforge has frozen active feature development of the Sley 1.x architecture.
- The Apache-2.0 1.x repository remains available for use, study, extension,
  experimentation, and forks.
- Active language research has moved to a clean machine-native Sley 2.x
  architecture.
- Sley 2.x preserves human governance while making direct human readability of
  the canonical raw program representation optional.
- Compatibility, migration tooling, release timing, and unreleased 2.x
  mechanisms are not promised.

## High-Confidence Facts

- In Sley 1.x, human-readable source remains the review projection.
- Compiler-exposed structure is the intended autonomous work surface.
- Public capability classes include structural inspection, planned change,
  diagnostics, authority checks, verification, provenance, traces, seals, and
  evidence-oriented handoff.
- The public branch includes a bounded read-only tool bridge, a staged-change
  guard, report-only structural comparison, release validation profiles, local
  transaction review/sealing, worker and adapter protocols, and release artifact
  verification surfaces.
- Deterministic host gates report authority state. Live host, provider,
  financial, deployment, publishing, and external actions follow the explicit
  operator authority around the workflow.
- The 2026-08-26 release-candidate inventory contains 99 report schemas, 187
  contract fixtures, 24 accepted corpus cases, 48 rejected corpus cases, 264
  integration checks, and 38 local v1 gate targets.
- The release-candidate validation record reports 38 of 38 v1 targets, 11 of 11
  release checks, and 4 of 4 public checks.
- The supported release artifact boundary is Linux x86_64 with unsigned
  provenance. This is a release candidate, not a production promotion.
- Sley has a self-hosted compiler. Its parser, checker, runtime, bootstrap, and report
  semantics are owned by Sley source and exercised through the verification
  surface.

## Public Proof Surface

The public repository proves a self-hosted Sley compiler, broad report and
contract surfaces, language-owned semantic execution, and a passing local v1
gate. Its schema, fixture, corpus, integration, manifest, and source-comparison
artifacts make the current implementation directly inspectable.

## Claim Discipline

- Use the preferred description above for ordinary product references.
- Pair strong category or historical claims with the public evidence, language
  specification, contract reference, release record, and primary-source
  comparison packet.
- Treat controlled K1/K3 workflow evidence as bounded evidence for the measured
  workflow, not as a general benchmark.
- Keep live external action, private implementation details, authorship
  provenance, and broad historical comparisons tied to direct public evidence.
- Do not infer unreleased Sley 2.x syntax, encoding, implementation, benchmarks,
  compatibility, migration tooling, roadmap, release timing, or support
  commitments.

## Relationship To ZJX

Sley is the structural programming language. ZJX is the lossless archive and
evidence-retention system. Their public product surfaces are separate.

ZJX: https://zjx.greyforge.tech/

Autonomy, Engineered.
